text:
Kai Chen: Heads up — saw 3 OOMs hit prod at ~10:42 UTC after we flipped kernel_selector to auto-kernel-v2. Flamegraphs/pprof attached. Memory climbs ~20% in the tokenization/workspace path when batch_size > 8. We need an emergency mitigation playbook that we can run in the next 15–30m.

Maya Patel: :eyes: ok. Short-term (what I'd run now, in order):
1) Pin kernel_selector back to legacy for the affected runtime pools (canary then all).
2) Route override: limit max_batch_size to 4 for high-concurrency routes.
3) Enable aggressive KV eviction (ttl=30s / size-based shedding).
4) Enable buffer_reuse=true runtime flag to avoid extra allocations.
5) Apply circuit-breaker rule: reject requests with seq_len > 1024 / requests > 20k tokens.
I'll paste the exact commands.

Jose Rivera: Commands I ran last time for a similar spike:
```bash
# rollback kernel selector for pool "gpu-prod-a"
curl -sS -X POST "https://admin.internal/api/v1/runtime/pools/gpu-prod-a/flags" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"kernel_selector":"legacy"}'

# route override to cap batch size
curl -sS -X PATCH "https://admin.internal/api/v1/routes/route-embed/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"max_batch_size":4, "batching_enabled":true}'

# enable aggressive kv eviction
curl -sS -X POST "https://admin.internal/api/v1/kv/eviction" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"pool":"gpu-prod-a","policy":"ttl","ttl_seconds":30}'

# flip buffer reuse and workspace size hint
curl -sS -X POST "https://admin.internal/api/v1/runtime/flags" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"buffer_reuse":true, "workspace_size_hint": "medium"}'

# set circuit breaker for oversized requests
curl -sS -X POST "https://admin.internal/api/v1/runtime/circuit-breakers" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"pool":"gpu-prod-a","max_seq_len":1024,"max_output_tokens":20000,"fail_fast":true}'
```

Olivia Zhang: I'll attach the quick pprof/heap snapshot steps so we can collect evidence during mitigation:
```bash
# collect pprof from the runtime instance
ssh runtime@gpu-prod-a-12 'curl -sS http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/heap?seconds=30' -o heap.pb
pprof -pdf runtime-binary heap.pb > heap.pdf
# upload
aws s3 cp heap.pdf s3://redwood-inference-prod-artifacts/oom-debug/1945006789-heap.pdf
```
I'll start one snapshot against a canary instance and upload link here.

InfraBot: Incident created: INC-1945006789 — oom spike after kernel_selector change. Playbook attached: oom-mitigation-v2. Assigned: eng-runtime oncall.

Maya Patel: Order of operations suggestion (minimal blast radius):
- 00–03m: set circuit-breaker + route override (fast, no deploy).
- 03–10m: enable buffer_reuse + aggressive KV eviction (runtime flags).
- 10–20m: pin kernel_selector for canary pool and monitor. If stable, roll to remaining pools.
- If OOMs continue: drain and restart workers with smaller workspace_size and collect heap.

Kai Chen: Running 1–4 now against canary pool (gpu-prod-a-canary). Will post results. If anyone can watch tracing/SLIs: look at p99 GPU mem and allocator fragmentation metric (allocator_frag_ratio).

Jose Rivera: One note — when we flipped auto-kernel-v2 earlier it enabled an eager workspace path that preallocates per-batch workspace. If we drop max_batch_size and enable buffer_reuse that usually avoids the prealloc spike. Also bumping kv eviction reduces memory pressure from long-lived chat sessions.

Olivia Zhang: Uploaded initial pprof: https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-inference-prod-artifacts/oom-debug/1945006789-heap.pdf (only canary). Looks like peak is from workspace_allocator::reserve > tokenization path.

Maya Patel: If the canary pins cleanly, we should prepare a quick rollback PR to permanently set the selector back while we run a deeper perf investigation. Also file a perf-regression ticket linking this pprof + flamegraph.

Kai Chen: Can confirm canary metrics are improving after flags flip — p99 mem down ~18% after c. 5m. Keeping changes staged for 20m and then will decide on full roll. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Maya Patel: Thanks — I'll coordinate the rollback PR and post the mitigation checklist in the incident doc.

Kai Chen: Closing loop here when done.
